title: GCS-01: Unauthorized Remote Session Detected — 915 MHz Link Compromise

fields.logSource: C2 Link Controller / 915 MHz Radio Logs

lines.msg: Remote session established via 915 MHz link from IP 192.168.100.22 (not in Group’s approved vendor list). Session ID: 0x9E2D4F. Command: set_home_point(43.1724°N, 77.5631°W). Command: modify_flight_path(waypoint 7 → 150m E, 120m N). Source: not in Kit Log (FOM-4). No MFA or 2FA recorded. Session terminated at 09:13:50.
RTK-1 Base (SM-L1) received external GPS signal update from 10.17.40.11 (lodge Wi-Fi). GPS fix lost on RTK-1 and UAS-11 simultaneously.
Session terminated. No active connection. GCS-01 firmware mismatch (03.2026-C) detected. Expected: 03.2026-B. Found: 03.2026-C.
Firmware mismatch detected in C2 link controller (GCS-01). OEM app attempted to re-pair with GCS-12 (MAC: 915-0A-1F-3C-7D-4E) due to configuration drift. No record of GCS-12 in fleet or baseline.
RTK-1 and aircraft GNSS both lost fix under clear sky. DAA-1 and GCS-02 telemetry disagree on aircraft position.
New device entry in GCS-02 device list: GCS-12 (MAC: 915-0A-1F-3C-7D-4E). No record of GCS-12 in fleet or baseline.
OEM app on GCS-02 prompted: 'Device ID mismatch. Re-pair required. New device ID: GCS-12. Accept?' RPIC did not initiate command.

instructorNote: This is a critical clue confirming the attacker’s entry point via GCS-01. The TL must immediately validate the firmware mismatch and initiate managed SOC reporting.
